\mxunit{enrichment-modular-solutions}{Congruences and last digits}
\mxsubtitle{High school · number theory \textperiodcentered{} Worked solutions \textperiodcentered{} 03}

\begin{exercise}
Find the remainder of $-37$ modulo 8.
\end{exercise}
\begin{solution}
$-37 = 8 \times  (-5) + 3$, so the remainder is 3.
\end{solution}

\begin{exercise}
Find the last digit of $7^{2026}$.
\end{exercise}
\begin{solution}
The cycle is $7,9,3,1$ and $2026 \equiv  2$ (mod 4). The last digit is 9.
\end{solution}

\begin{exercise}
Prove that an integer square is never congruent to 2 modulo 3.
\end{exercise}
\begin{solution}
An integer is congruent to 0, 1 or 2. The corresponding squares are 0, 1 and $4 \equiv  1$ modulo 3.
\end{solution}

\begin{exercise}
Solve $3x \equiv  1$ (mod 7).
\end{exercise}
\begin{solution}
$3 \times  5 = 15 \equiv  1$. Multiplying by 5 gives $x \equiv  5$ (mod 7). Conversely, every such value works.
\end{solution}

\begin{problem}[Investigate, justify, conclude]
An integer N is congruent to 2 modulo 3 and to 3 modulo 5. Write $N = 3k + 2$, determine k modulo 5, then give all solutions modulo 15. Which solutions from 0 to 100 inclusive are even?
\end{problem}
\begin{solution}
$3k + 2 \equiv  3$ (mod 5), so $3k \equiv  1$ and $k \equiv  2$ (mod 5), since $3 \times  2 \equiv  1$. Thus $N = 15t + 8$. In $[0 ; 100]$ the values are $8,23,38,53,68,83,98$. The even values are $8,38,68,98$. Substitution verifies both congruences for every integer t.
\end{solution}
